newsitem.title: UK: MOTOR RACING-LOLA BOSS CONFIRMS LIQUIDATION.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-LOLA BOSS CONFIRMS LIQUIDATION.

text.p: Briton Eric Broadley, the boss of the Lola Formula One motor racing team, confirmed on Tuesday that the outfit had gone into liquidation following Grand Prix failures this season.
Broadley's two cars, driven by Brazilian Ricardo Rosset and Italian Vincenzo Sospiri, failed to qualify for the season opening Australian Grand Prix in March after a lack of development and testing.

Three weeks later, he withdrew the team from the sport on the eve of the Brazilian Grand Prix with debts believed to be in the region of three million pounds ($4.9 million) after a leading sponsor pulled out.
Broadley had hoped to resurrect the team with different sponsors but, at a creditors meeting on Monday, no rescue package was forthcoming.
Although Broadley did not wish to comment on the matter, he did make it clear that the future of Lola Cars, a separate company that sells racing machinery around the world, was not under threat.
